newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bank industry wants merger freedom.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bank industry wants merger freedom.

text.p: The Australian Bankers Association (ABA) said on Monday that the government should have the power to veto finance industry mergers but in most cases the restrictive "six pillars" merger policy should be regarded as redundant.

"The Treasurer should have the power to allow, or disallow, a merger between banks or between a bank and another financial institution," the ABA said in its submission to the Wallis financial system inquiry.

"This power should only be used for prudential reasons, on the advice of the relevant regulatory authorities, and not to pursue competition policy objectives where no significant prudential issue is at stake," the ABA said.
"Such an approach would among other things make the "six pillars" policy of the previous government redundant," it said.
The Wallis Inquiry will hand its report to the government by March next year, with further industry deregulation a key topic for consideration.

Banking analysts believe the major banks support the scrapping of the "six pillars" policy, a defacto approach taken by the government and regulators which blocks mergers among the "Big Four" banks or with the two largest life offices.
But the smaller banks, which are also members of the ABA, are likely to argue in the inquiry that there should be some continued safeguard against their takeover by the majors.
